title: Working Out the Employer Allowance Placed on an Employee Meal Account for a Grant Period
content:
The employer allowance placed on an Employee Meal Account for a grant period is worked out from the plan the account is held on, from the employer's dining programme at the account's site and from what the account's own ledger shows has already been granted and spent.

## 1. The base grant

The base grant is the grant amount printed against the meal plan the account is held on.

## 2. The availability share

The availability share is the whole of the grant period.

## 3. What is carried in

Nothing is carried into the new lot from allowance the account already holds.

## 4. The grant period ceiling

The grant period ceiling is the grant ceiling printed against the meal plan the account is held on.

## 5. Allowance already standing

Nothing already on the account is treated as standing against the new lot.

## 6. Assembling the lot

The allowance granted is worked out in this order and in no other: the base grant is taken at the availability share and rounded to two decimal places at that step; the amount carried in is added to that figure; the sum is then held to the grant period ceiling; and the allowance already standing is taken off last, the result never being read as less than nothing. The figure is rounded to two decimal places at the end, over and above the rounding named above.

## Worked through on hypothetical figures

Suppose the plan the account is held on prints, for this illustration, a grant amount of $11.00 and a grant ceiling of $11.00 for one grant period.

The base grant is $11.00. The availability share is the whole of the grant period, so taking the base grant at it leaves $11.00, rounded at that step. Nothing is carried in, so the sum is $11.00. Held to the grant period ceiling of $11.00 it stays $11.00. Nothing is treated as already standing, so nothing comes off last. Rounded once more at the end, the lot granted is $11.00.

Suppose instead the same plan printed a grant amount of $11.00 against a grant ceiling of $9.00. The sum of $11.00 would be held down to the ceiling of $9.00, and the lot granted would be $9.00.


## How a window of calendar months is counted

A window of calendar months in this policy runs back from the day the account is worked and never from the turn of a named month: an entry falls inside such a window while fewer than that many whole months have gone by since the day it was booked, a whole month going by only when the same day of the month comes round again, so an entry exactly that many whole months old falls outside it, and an entry booked after the day the account is worked falls outside it too.
